newsitem.title: UK: Dollar/yen resilient in face of Japan's trade data.
newsitem.headline: Dollar/yen resilient in face of Japan's trade data.

text.p: The dollar was little changed against the yen, resilient in the face of a report which showed Japan's trade surplus surged anew in May.

Traders briefly drove the dollar below 113 yen in Asia after Japan's Finance Ministry said the trade surplus rose 222.2 percent in May from a year earlier to 738.27 billion yen and reported a 93 percent increase in the surplus with the U.S. in the same period.
The U.S. currency recovered, though, as traders were wary of adding to their short dollar positions before a meeting of the Group of Seven leading industrial nations later this week.

"When the market focuses so much on something, things tend to get overdone in the run up to the event," said Juergen Lindemann, a senior trader at IBJ. "People were already long of yen and when the market tried to take the dollar below 113 last night, the profit takers were lurking around the corner."
The dollar was at 113.46/51 yen at 0750 GMT from 113.27/37 late Tuesday in Europe. It was at 1.7236/41 from 1.7336/46 late yesterday.
A U.S. official in Tokyo said Wednesday the trade data reinforced American concern about a renewed widening in Japan's trade surplus.

The official noted, however, that Japan has pledged to promote domestic demand-led growth in order to avoid a resurgence in its current account surplus. Traders aren't looking for G7 officials to say anything more specific than that when they meet in Denver Friday, Saturday and Sunday.
"The fundamentals are overwhelmingly against dollar/yen and there is no way it can stay up here," said Peter von Maydell, the senior currency economist at UBS.
"The G7 might be an excuse for people to wait to do something, but the only thing you can expect is for them to say something about the currency volatility we have seen recently."
